articles.title: Making Marie Antoinette review – sweet Coppola home movie reveals the family business
articles.summary: Shot by Sofia’s mother Eleanor this documentary shows something of the strain of shooting a period piece, but is a far cry from the tumultuous portrait of her husband in Hearts of Darkness.
body: I t is 20 years since the release of Sofia Coppola’s Marie Antoinette starring Kirsten Dunst; it is a supportively unjudging, unironised study of the queen’s early years before the 1789 revolution, lavishly and accurately costumed, shot on location at Versailles and based on the Antonia Fraser biography – but also subversively and amusingly using pop tracks from the 70s and 80s on the soundtrack. It got a storm of booing from French critics, reportedly annoyed at the way their history had been reduced to a music video and fashion shoot with no French actors involved. Or hardly any.
points: Shot by Sofia’s mother Eleanor this documentary shows something of the strain of shooting a period piece, but is a far cry from the tumultuous portrait of her husband in Hearts of Darkness.

articles.title: Ghosts: The Possession of Button House review – new levels of giddiness unleashed in spooky spin-off
articles.summary: Picking up not long after the events of the final episode of the BBC’s haunted house comedy, this glorious new film is every bit as warm and comforting as the TV sitcom. What on earth is happening at Button House? Kitty has tasered a police officer.
body: Often when British sitcoms get a spin-off what happens is the gag-to-runtime ratio dips. But breaking out of the 30-minute episode structure seems to have freed up the writers to unleash new levels of giddiness with added spoonfuls of silliness. The jokes keep coming, and it’s every bit as warm and comforting as on TV.

To say anything about the plot would ruin the fun. (I watched with a nine-year-old who hooted throughout.) It really is a delight. My only complaint is the timing: if the BBC was serious about public service it would have waited a couple of months and put this on telly at Christmas for a bit of genuine festive cheer.

articles.title: ‘Industry,’ ‘Doctor Who’ Producer Jane Tranter on Resisting Trends, Centering Women and Telling Stories About ‘People Being Accepted for Who They Choose to Be’
articles.summary: “Industry” and “Doctor Who” producer Jane Tranter has made a career of going against the grain, and at Rome’s MIA Market on Tuesday, she told European producers that the only way to survive in uncertain times is to “go in the opposite direction of everyone else’s traffic.” “If everyone else is…
body: Opening up about her early days in the industry in the 1990s, Tranter recalled her time as a drama script editor at ITV franchise Carlton Television, when she was told that “no drama that had a female protagonist was ever going to draw an audience.” Before long, however, she joined a cohort of powerhouse female executives who would reshape the face of British television.

“I didn’t think that I was leading a revolution. I just thought that I was going to make drama that I wanted to watch,” she said. “And if it’s drama that I want to watch, the drama should be inclusive of all. And in particular, I wanted to watch drama that had women in it.”

The wide-ranging conversation touched on some of the iconic series that Tranter helped shepherd to the screen, from the HBO crime drama “The Night Of” (“It took two Obama presidencies to see it through”) to the multi-Emmy-winning “Succession” (“It was the best writers’ room I have ever experienced”) to “His Dark Materials,” the HBO fantasy adventure series that aired from 2019-2022 and “had a heartbeat to it that was speaking to where the world was going.”

articles.title: ‘Father’s House,’ Starring David Dencik and Trine-Dyrholm, Picked Up by DR Sales Ahead of Tallinn Competition
articles.summary: Copenhagen-based DR Sales, the international distributor of Oscar-winning doc “Mr Nobody Against Putin” and Sundance winner “A New Kind of Wilderness,” has boarded Denmark’s “Father’s House,” starring David Dencik (“No Time to Die,” “The Chestnut Man”) and Trine Dyrholm (“The Danish Woman,” “Queen…
body: “Father’s House” is co-directed by multi-awarded doc specialists Andreas Koefoed (“The Lost Leonardo,” “Music for Black Pigeons”), Eva Mulvad (“Enemies of Happiness,” “The Good Life”) and editor Adam Nielsen (“The Investigation,” “The Letter Room”).

“We have been very excited about this project for some time. Once we saw the first cut, we were all blown away by how powerful and original the film is,” said DR Sales Executive Producer Kim Christiansen.

A distinctive mix of fiction, documentary and making off, “Father’s House” (“Faderhuset”) looks at manipulation, abuse and often violence inside the radical Danish Christian sect Faderhuset, as three former members expose the inner workings of the now defunct sect where exorcism and speaking in tongues and militant Christianity were, reportedly, part of everyday life.
Defining moments in the lives of the three characters within that closed sect are brought back to life via reenactments from established actors, under the guidance of the real former members.

articles.title: ‘Pirates of the Caribbean’ Secret Cinema Immersive Stage Show Casts George Maguire as Jack Sparrow, Extends London Run
articles.summary: Olivier winner George Maguire will play Captain Jack Sparrow in “Disney’s Pirates of the Caribbean: The Immersive Adventure,” the London stage production from Secret Cinema and TodayTix. Phil Daniels, known for “Quadrophenia,” “EastEnders” and Blur’s “Parklife,” will play Captain Barbossa.
body: No earlier stage version of the franchise has been fully immersive, and the show marks a change of approach for Secret Cinema. Live storytelling leads the show. Instead of screening the whole of “Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl,” the production uses selected clips from the film alongside large set pieces. Over two hours, audiences can roam the sets, meet characters and take part in the story, with stunts and a live band.

The creative team includes two-time Emmy winner Jason Sherwood as production designer. His credits include live broadcasts of the Oscars and “Rent Live.” Kait Kerrigan, who wrote the book for Broadway’s “The Great Gatsby,” is the theatrical adaptor. Olivier winner Alan Williams handles music supervision, arrangements and orchestrations. Stuart Burt is casting director, Susan Kulkarni designs costumes, Helen Keane of Campbell Young Associates designs wigs, hair and makeup, and Alex Payne is fight director.
points: Olivier winner George Maguire will play Captain Jack Sparrow in “Disney’s Pirates of the Caribbean: The Immersive Adventure,” the London stage production from Secret Cinema and TodayTix.

articles.title: Thai Pop Star Jeff Satur Signs With Universal Music Southeast Asia, Sets 2027 Album and World Tour
articles.summary: Thai singer-songwriter and actor Jeff Satur, whose music has passed 2 billion streams, has signed with Universal Music Southeast Asia (UM SEA), the regional division of Universal Music Group, as he pushes to take T-pop to a global audience.
body: “At this point in my career, it was important for me to find a partner that truly understands my vision, one that can help me bring my ideas to life without losing what makes them mine,” Satur said. “I’m excited for Saturn to meet the Universe and begin the next chapter of creating without borders, because at its heart, music has always been my universal language.”

Satur, who also produces, is known for tracks including “Fade,” “Dum Dum,” “Hide,” “Ghost” and “Black Tie,” and has built a fan following across Asia, the U.S. and Latin America. His 2025 Red Giant Tour played Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines, Japan, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Brazil, Chile, Mexico and Peru. At home, it included two sold-out shows at Bangkok’s Impact Arena, Thailand’s largest indoor arena.

This year, Satur was the first Thai artist to appear at Global Spin Live, a conversation-and-performance event at L.A.’s Grammy Museum, and to play live on “Good Day New York,” the TV program on New York’s WNYW Fox 5.

articles.title: You Can See Everything mania lifts viewership for The Dropout by 186%
articles.summary: The hit Elizabeth Holmes documentary led to increased interest in the award-winning narrative series on Hulu as well as Bad Blood, a 2018 book on the scandal. ‘Stranger than stranger-than-fiction’: how Lance Oppenheim made the year’s two buzziest films.
body: Interest in Elizabeth Holmes and the Theranos fraud scandal has surged amid buzz for You Can See Everything, the record-breaking documentary on the disgraced former CEO.

Viewership for The Dropout, the 2022 Hulu series starring Amanda Seyfried as Holmes, surged by 186% in September compared with the month prior, according to Variety, after the announcement on 6 September of the previously secret film’s first teaser.
Viewership nearly doubled again during the week of 12 October, increasing 92% over the week prior in the days before the film’s 16 October premiere.

Additionally, Bad Blood, the 2018 book by journalist John Carreyrou detailing the inner workings of Holmes’s fraudulent empire and the whistleblowers who exposed her, returned to the New York Times bestseller list.

articles.title: Ali G is back. But is the character past its sell-by date?
articles.summary: Borat and Bruno creator Sacha Baron Cohen returns as Ali G, more than two decades after the release of Ali G Indahouse.
body: "This is the biggest gathering of cultural appropriators in history," Sacha Baron Cohen tells the camera in his parody of a street accent.

Behind him, hundreds of fans cram onto a London Underground escalator, all wearing Ali G's trademark yellow shell suit and skullcap. Baron Cohen shouts the character's catchphrases through a megaphone, with the crowd enthusiastically finishing each one.

Earlier this month, more than 300 fans attended an official Ali G lookalike competition, ferried around London on an open-top bus that stopped at landmarks including Big Ben, Leicester Square and Covent Garden.
The stunt was promotion for an upcoming sequel to 2002 film Ali G Indahouse - called Ali G: Who iz I? - which hits cinemas on Friday.

articles.title: Camel Racing, a Sect and Workplace Democracy: Tallinn Fest Sets Docs Lineup, Special Screenings
articles.summary: The 30th edition of the Estonian festival also unveils Stephen Frears' 'Dangerous Liaisons' and Tim Blake Nelson's 'The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd' among its latest program additions.
body: The Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) unveiled the selection of documentaries in its Doc@PÖFF International and Baltic competitions on Wednesday, adding to the program for its 30th edition, taking place Nov. 6-2. For the second year in a row, Baltic documentaries and feature films will compete in separate programs.

Marianna Kaat, the curator of the Doc@PÖFF International and Baltic competitions, said: “This year, I was particularly struck by filmmakers finding fresh ways to tell their stories, opening up new possibilities for documentary cinema and its role in defending our sense of reality. These films ask us to look more closely, question our assumptions and resist easy explanations. In a world where so much comes to us already interpreted, that feels especially necessary.”

One of the docs, Father’s House, uses actors, namely Trine Dyrholm, David Dencik and Emma Sehested Høeg, for reenactments of former members’ experiences inside the controlling Christian sect. Those who lived through them advise the performers, share their memories and watch as some of their most traumatic experiences unfold before them.

articles.title: ‘It’s important that Michael’s voice is heard’: Jaafar Jackson says second biopic of his uncle will cover sexual abuse allegations
articles.summary: The star of Michael, the most commercially successful biopic of all time, has said sequel will give airtime to point-of-view of late singer. Of all the criticisms levelled at the authorised biopic of Michael Jackson released earlier this year, the most persistent was that Antoine Fuqua’s film…
body: In part, this was due to a legal clause, only spotted late in production, which stipulated that one of the men who accused Jackson of abusing them as a boy could never be depicted in a fictionalised account of the period.
A sequence involving a police raid at the Neverland ranch was cut, $50m (£37m) of reshoots were funded by the Jackson family, and the narrative was curtailed early.
However, the enormous box office response to the film, which recently overtook Oppenheimer as the highest-grossing biopic of all time, has meant a sequel is inevitable.

Speaking to Variety, star Jaafar Jackson – the nephew of the man he plays – downplayed the first film’s production woes, saying: “I’ve heard many stories from other actors about how much you shoot on a project that doesn’t make it into the final picture.
